text:
**I’d pick Starling as your main UK account.** If you want one place for your salary, bills and everyday spending, it’s the best all-rounder of the three: no monthly fee or minimum pay-in, free Direct Debits and standing orders, cheque deposits in the app, and an arranged overdraft if you qualify. You can also pay in cash at the Post Office; the first £1,000 per calendar year is free, then Starling charges 0.7% on the excess. ([starlingbank.com](https://www.starlingbank.com/current-account/compare-best-bank-accounts/?utm_source=openai))

**I’d choose Chase instead if you’ll earn the cashback without changing your habits.** It pays 2% on eligible UK spending, including groceries, eating out, everyday transport and fuel, capped at £20 a month. To qualify the following month, you need to keep at least £1,000 across Chase savers **every day** of the qualifying month and make at least 15 card payments or Direct Debits that month. At £500 of eligible spending, that’s £10 back. Chase now accepts free cash deposits at PayPoint, but it doesn’t accept cheques or offer an arranged overdraft. ([chase.co.uk](https://www.chase.co.uk/gb/en/support/where-can-i-earn-cashback/?utm_source=openai))

**I’d choose Revolut if you regularly manage money in multiple currencies**, rather than just wanting a card for holidays. Starling already charges no fee for overseas card spending or ATM withdrawals. Revolut Standard has a £1,000 monthly exchange allowance, with a 1% fee above it. Before moving your salary, check **Details** in the Revolut app: eligible deposits with **Revolut Bank UK Ltd** have FSCS protection up to £120,000 per person, whereas a **Revolut Ltd** e-money balance is safeguarded instead. ([starlingbank.com](https://www.starlingbank.com/current-account/compare-best-bank-accounts/?utm_source=openai))

So unless Chase’s qualifying rules already fit your routine or you regularly handle several currencies, **go with Starling**.
